subject: railgunCarrier
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: six-wheeled railgun carrier braced on stabiliser legs.
Style: low-poly sci-fi military.
reasoning:
I'm planning a single, reasonably compact TypeScript module for the vehicle, deciding it doesn't need a full creature skeleton since vehicles can be static objects, but adding a few joints for the hull, turret, and barrel to allow some movement.

Now I'm working out the actual dimensions and part placement -- hull length and width, wheel positions and sizes using cylinder geometry, and tire/hub/rim details. I'm also figuring out the stabilizer legs, deciding where they brace against the hull and ground relative to the wheel positions.

Building the hull geometry...

I'm placing the windshield as a slanted plane with a teal glass tint, adding side windows similarly, then moving to the rear engine deck with vented texture, a central turret ring lathe geometry, and a railgun mount cradle.

Now I'm positioning the railgun barrel assembly over the cab, using two parallel square-section rail boxes spanning roughly 12m, pivoting from a joint beneath the turret and aiming forward along +Z.

Working out the rail insulators and coil rings next -- spacing dark/glow blocks along the rails and using a hollow lathed band as a ring shape around each coil position.

Now I'm shifting to the turret body, planning a hexagonal lathed base ring plus a boxy housing with sloped sides built from an extruded profile, along with capacitor cylinders and glow strips as accent details.

Then I'm mapping out the joint hierarchy: hull root, turret parented to hull, gun parented to turret with its firing direction, stabilizer joints, and six wheel joints along the x-axis parented to hull, deciding which ones need role labels like "leg" and which can be left unassigned.

For the wheel parts I'm attaching them to their joints in model space, noting that joint orientation doesn't matter much since parts use their own position and direction. For paint, I'm designing an olive military finish with mottled camo patches blending drab and olive tones, plus a dirt gradient that darkens toward the bottom and lightens near the top.

Now I'm planning the decal textures — windshield glass with reflections, a hex emblem with unit number, hazard stripes, grille vents, maybe a radar dish and capacitor label — aiming for around six distinct texture planes to layer onto the model.

I'm sketching a decal helper that places a textured plane at a position with a given facing direction and up vector, then working out where the emblem goes on the hull sides and how fender plates bridge over the wheels without clipping into them.

Now I'm laying out the equipment bay as a box spanning the body width and height, positioning it between the chassis and cab sections, and planning a turret ring on top near the rear.

Still defining chamfered box coordinates...

Now thinking about the rear details: adding exhaust stack cylinders at the rear corners, a grille decal and lights on the rear bay face, plus a stowed digging spade plate angled down near the back of the vehicle.

For the cab, I'm sketching headlights as glowing yellow boxes on the front face, along with an armored visor, front bumper box, and tow hooks.

I'm adding roof details like antenna whips, a sensor dome, a radar dish on a rear mast, and an amber beacon light. Then I'm working out the chassis layout, positioning a front bumper box and figuring out wheel and stabilizer leg placements along the z-axis.

Now I'm placing the stabilizer legs between the wheel gaps, attaching upper struts from the chassis sides down to foot pads on the ground, with a thinner piston rod running alongside each leg.

For the feet, I'm adding a triangular brace, a cylindrical pad, and a ball-joint sphere where the leg meets the ground, plus a hydraulic housing and mounting bracket at the hull. Next I'm positioning the turret ring on top of the bay, setting its joint pivot point before building out the turret shape itself.

Now I'm shaping the turret body as an extruded profile with angled top plates, and sketching where the gun mount and cheek plates attach near the trunnion joint.

Placing the turret top at y 3.5, I'm positioning the railgun assembly on top with twin rails sitting higher at y 3.9-4.05, running from the rear of the turret out to a muzzle around z 7.3, giving an overall length near 12 meters. I'm laying out the rail cross-section with two side rails flanking a dark center core, plus a muzzle brake and coil rings up front.

Working out the coil ring geometry now, sizing them as hollow lathe rings spaced around the rails without touching them, with inner radius around 0.5 and outer around 0.66, spaced roughly every 0.7 units along the barrel length.

Adding copper coloring with cyan glow strips embedded along the rail inner faces, plus two large cylindrical capacitor banks mounted on either side of the turret.

Positioning the capacitor cylinders with dome end caps, then adding power cable sweeps connecting the capacitors to the rail using catmull curves, mirrored for symmetry. Now I'm placing the commander's cupola, roof hatch, sight, and a front sensor camera pod with a glowing lens, plus a turret emblem decal.

Deciding where the hazard/number decal goes on the turret side, adjusting the capacitor position slightly so it doesn't overlap the decal zone. Now I'm working out the wheel geometry -- building a tire as a lathed profile with tread detailing to avoid a plain smooth cylinder look.

Writing lathe profile...

I want the wheel to roll convincingly on the ground, so I'm checking whether the lathe segmentation creates a flat face or sharp vertex at the bottom, and confirming the small gap from floor contact is negligible either way. Then I'm sketching the hub as a steel cylinder with six lug nuts ringed around the axle.

Still placing lug nuts...

I'm adding suspension rods connecting the hull to each wheel hub, positioned so they're visible beneath the chassis, and considering whether to skip a central drive shaft and add mud flaps instead.

Thinking through fenders and side armor plates between wheels, deciding whether to use a paneled texture with rivets for added detail at a reasonable scale for the vehicle size.

Calculating that at this texel density, fine rivets and seams would be nearly invisible anyway, so I'll skip the paneled rivet approach and rely on flat geometry with camo-pattern paint instead, bumping paint resolution to 2048. I'll add simpler surface details like hatches, handles, and vents on the cab and bay using basic box shapes rather than fine rivet geometry.

Now I'm planning the parts list: tool boxes along the bay sides, jerry cans at the rear, aiming for roughly 150 parts total with 6 textures. I'm setting up a box-generation helper for placing geometry with position, bone, and rotation options, plus mirroring loops for left/right symmetry, and defining the joint hierarchy (hull root, turret, gun, three wheel joints per side, stabilizer arms) before starting on the hull chassis extrusion.

For textures, I'm sketching out SVG designs: a tinted window with diagonal reflection streaks, a circular emblem with a chevron star and "07" text, yellow-black hazard stripes generated procedurally, a dark grille with horizontal slats, and a "DANGER HV" warning label with a lightning bolt, while skipping extras like HUD screens or camera lens details.

I'm also placing a "MK-IV RAILGUN" text texture on both sides of the barrel, mirrored correctly so it reads right from either angle, bringing the total texture count to six including the headlight. Now I'm positioning a windshield plane along the cab's sloped front, figuring out its center point, dimensions, and orientation relative to the local up-axis.

Then I'm working out the side cab window placements, matching their size and position to the cab's profile between the roof and front slope, and checking that the front wheel position doesn't overlap the cab's side geometry.

Now I'm sizing and positioning the fender plates and skirt walls around the wheels, making sure there's a small gap above the wheel top and that these pieces stay clear of the chassis and cab edges.

Checking the fender spans against each leg's z position confirms both legs land cleanly in the gaps between fenders. Now I'm working out the leg geometry itself—defining the attachment point on the chassis side wall, the foot position, and the upper strut rod connecting them.

Still refining pad geometry...

Now I'm adding the ball joint, glowing headlight boxes near the cab front, and a grille decal on the chassis face.

I'm placing the headlights and grille with spacing that fits within the cab's width, then adding a front bumper box positioned against the chassis, checking wheel clearance, and considering a hazard stripe decal on the bumper's front face.

Now I'm working on the rear assembly: a spade plate extruded behind the chassis that reaches down to the ground, connected by angled hydraulic ram rods running from the chassis to the spade, plus red rear light boxes positioned on the bay's rear face.

Adding exhaust stacks and vent details...

I'm placing a radar mast and antenna whips on the cab roof, with thin flexible rods and ball tips, plus a hatch between the turret and cab.

Now I'm adding a radar dish to the mast, shaping a parabolic lathe profile tilted toward the front, and checking that it clears the gun's line of sight and barrel position.

I'm also adding cab roof details — beacon, sensor dome, hatch — and a cradle bracket with support posts to hold the barrel in travel mode, making sure the geometry fits beneath the rails.

Working out the trunnion cheeks on the turret bone, placing them slightly outside the rail width so they don't overlap, then figuring the rail length as a long frustum box spanning roughly 10 units along z.

Adding glow details...

Finishing the lathe outline for the glow ring, then moving to the gun's rear breech block with an energy glow slit and power conduits, plus turret details like camera pods and a cupola with a dome on top.

Now I'm placing emblem decals on the bay side walls and turret sides, figuring out their positions and sizing relative to the bay opening, plus adding a label decal and hazard markings near the rear step.

Defining color constants for the different materials—dark metal, steel, chrome, rubber, yellow, copper—and confirming ground contact points sit at y=0 for wheels, pads, and spade. I'm also adding an extruded armor wedge to the turret front and setting up helper functions using vector interpolation for the construction code.

Setting up joints: hull root, turret and gun positions parented appropriately, then writing box and cylinder helper functions for building the geometry...

Writing plane helper...

Now I'm defining a wheel function that creates a joint on the hull and builds a tire using a lathe profile, symmetric across the x-axis.

For the hub assembly, I'm adding a steel cylinder core, a chrome rim plate, a small domed cap, and six lug nuts positioned radially around the hub center.

I'll just keep individual lug nut spheres rather than merging geometry since the part count stays manageable, and skip adding tread grooves to the tire, using a mottled dark rubber tint for a slight grime effect instead. For the axle, I'm placing a short rigid rod connecting the hull to the wheel position.

Now I'm adding a differential housing sphere at the axle center, sized so it sits visibly below the chassis without clipping into it, repeating this for each of the three axles. Then I'm moving on to writing out the full chassis extrusion profile and dimensions in code.

Still writing extrusion profiles...

Defining the turret polygon points and ring alignment, then laying out the capacitor cylinders and their mounting brackets on the turret sides.

Now I'm routing power cables as curved sweeps from the capacitors toward the breech rail, and positioning the rail's text plane along with the overlapping coil ring details.

I realize the coil rings would partially obscure a text label on the rail itself, so I'm reconsidering placement — instead putting the "MK-IV RAILGUN" label on the breech block's side face, where it won't clash with the ring geometry.

Working out the breech block dimensions and position relative to where the rails begin, then placing the text plane centered on its side at a scaled offset. Now adjusting the coil ring layout along the rail length, spacing them every 0.9 units starting near the turret cradle, checking that their radius doesn't awkwardly intersect the turret body, and considering adding a few larger rings toward the rear.

Checking that the support yoke placement near z=3.15 leaves enough clearance between the adjacent coil rings at 2.7 and 3.6. I'm adding a glow face offset for the rail rings, then defining a lathed muzzle ring near the barrel tip with a steel outline profile, plus small copper emitter caps capping the rail ends. Now I'm listing out all the glow elements needed: cab beacon, headlights, tail lights, rail glow, ring glow, and breech slit.

I want to add antenna whips and stowed gear -- deciding where to place toolboxes and jerrycans across the rear and middle fenders, sizing them as small boxes mounted on fender plates, while skipping front fender details and a rear ladder for simplicity.

Now I'm working out the lug nuts, hubcap dome, and wheel rim geometry -- positioning small cylinders around the hub circle and sizing the hub cap and rim plate dimensions...

Writing the window SVG...

Still building asset shapes for grille, label, and railgun text elements...

Writing hull paint shader with camo mottling and mud gradient effects...

Now I'm adding capacitor band coloring that alternates between brass and steel-blue tones based on position.
